newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks close firmer in steady, strong trade. [CORRECTED 22:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks close firmer in steady, strong trade. [CORRECTED 22:30 GMT]

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed higher in strong, steady trade as optimism and rises in second-tier shares offset some early profit-taking on leading blue chips, brokers said.
"The market was quiet today. Stocks were mostly stable," said one local broker.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 48 most-traded shares ended 0.14 percent higher at 11,361 points on volume totalling 880.5 million reais ($823 million).
(Corrects to 880.5 million reais from 880.5 billion reais.)

Brokers said Monday's trend was set by bellwether Telebras, whose benchmark preferred fluctuated between 147.40 reais and 150 reais before ending at 148.40 reais, a rise of 0.68 percent. Its common ended 0.37 percent up at 140 reais.
Despite some profit-taking, share prices were supported by continued strong flows of capital to Brazilian equities, they said.
Telebras' price was propped up by optimism ahead of the awarding of Brazil's B Band cellular concessions and speculation ahead of a June 16 options expiry.

The day's rise was led by bank Banespa, whose shares traded for the first time in seven sessions after being suspended pending the conclusion of a deal to transfer the former state bank to the federal government. 15.95 reais and its common closed 15.01 percent higher at 15.70 reais.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index of nine most-traded power stocks closed 0.31 percent up at 2,841 points, led by Minas Gerais state-owned power firm Cemig.
Cemig's preferred jumped 3.27 percent to 50.60 reais while its common ended 2.35 percent at 47.89 reais.
Among blue chips, Eletrobras preferred rose 0.76 percent at 531 reais.
Cia Vale do Rio Doce's preferred ended 0.63 percent higher at 23.50 reais, while state oil firm Petrobras' preferred closed 2.34 percent lower at 250 reais.
